conventions.convention: Translations use the cocharacter lattice Y: W_aff = Q∨ ⋊ W₀ and W_e = Y ⋊ W₀. Walls are α(v) = j. Alcoves retain the common root kernel, and Ω is the full alcove stabilizer, including central translations.
Parameters q_s are positive real and constant on extended conjugacy classes. The quadratic normalization is (T_s − q_s)(T_s + 1) = 0, with v_s = √q_s and N_s = v_s⁻¹T_s.

The exceptional Bernstein relation occurs for α ∈ 2X. Comparison with a fixed Iwahori–Matsumoto algebra requires attaching v′_α to the square-root parameter of H_{α,1}; an unattached formal scalar supplies no such comparison.
A positive signed crossing moves toward the chosen chamber D at infinity. Bernstein translations use dominant D and Θ_y = N_{t_λ}N_{t_μ}⁻¹ for y = λ − μ with λ and μ dominant.
Parabolic H_P retains the full lattice L = Y. Classification modules are nonzero, unital, complex and finite dimensional; weights are generalized Bernstein weights, and λ(t)(ℓ) = log|t(ℓ)|.

Tempered logarithmic weights lie in K_P, the negative simple-coroot cone. Strict position requires ν ∈ E^P and β(ν) > 0 outside P. The exponent retains every central real direction; for P = B the positivity inequalities are empty.

The selected group is SL₂(Q₃), with simply connected datum, Ω = 1, left Haar normalization μ(I) = 1 and an explicit AC assumption. The conclusion is a convolution-corner isomorphism and action on V^I, without a representation-category equivalence.

load_bearing.statement: For any reduced based root datum and positive extended-conjugacy-invariant affine parameters, with exceptional Bernstein parameters attached to the odd walls, Θ_y = N_{t_λ}N_{t_μ}⁻¹ is independent of the dominant decomposition y = λ − μ and multiplicative. Both ordered Bernstein families are bases, and θ_y ↦ Θ_y, N_s ↦ N_s defines an isomorphism from the attached formal Bernstein algebra to the Iwahori–Matsumoto algebra.

W_aff = Q∨ ⋊ W₀ is the Coxeter group on the base-alcove wall reflections, acts simply transitively on alcoves and has separating-wall length. Y ⋊ W₀ = W_aff ⋊ Ω, including empty roots and central directions. Wall parameters depend only on level parity, and the two parity values agree when α ∉ 2X.

H is right free over H_P with basis N_w for w ∈ W^P, and induction injects 1 ⊗ V. Its generalized weight multiset is the disjoint multiset union of w Wt(V). An irreducible H_P-module has one W_P-orbit of weights; a submodule generated by a generalized t-weight space has weights in W_Pt. Temperedness is preserved and reflected by induction, and real-exponent twists identify essentially tempered modules with tempered modules.

Every λ has a unique orthogonal decomposition λ = ν + η with ν = p(λ) ∈ C, P its simple-root zero set and η ∈ K_P. For ν ∈ C_P^{++}, η ∈ K_P and nonidentity w ∈ W^P, r(w(ν + η)) < ‖ν‖. For η′ ∈ E_P, r(ν + η′) ≥ ‖ν‖, with equality exactly when η′ ∈ K_P.

Signed gallery products E_D(g) are independent of the expression, including nonreduced expressions, and form a complex vector-space basis indexed by W_e. The independence assertion also holds for galleries beginning at another alcove, with framed endpoints retaining their group elements.

For a Langlands datum (P, σ) with exponent ν, I_P(σ) has a unique maximal proper submodule and unique irreducible quotient L(P, σ). In both modules the largest projection-norm value is ‖ν‖, and its generalized-weight subspace is canonically the injected σ as an H_P-module; every such weight projects to ν.

The rank-two Z₃-lattice homothety graph is a degree-four tree. SL₂(Q₃) preserves vertex types and is transitive on type-ordered edges, with stabilizer I as displayed. I-orbits on edges are indexed by alternating words in s₀,s₁, with 3ⁿ edges for word length n, and identify with the corresponding double cosets.

published_dependencies.used_for: Perfect lattice duality, reflection formulas, reduced root data and Weyl-group conventions.
Finite Weyl action, essential Euclidean realization, chambers, simple-root signs and inversion-number length.
Symmetric Hecke normalization, odd-edge parameter constraints and conjugacy of simple generators.
Least vanishing geometric-sum definition and the root-of-unity order formula.
Integer-level affine walls, reflection signs and coroot translations.
Essential affine Coxeter presentation, simple transitivity, wall conjugacy and separating-wall length.
Finite gallery moves and rank-two dihedral wall cycles underlying signed-product independence.
Standard-basis freeness after arbitrary commutative coefficient specialization, without a flatness assumption.
Reduced-word braid independence and reduction by braid moves and adjacent cancellations.
Identification of Z₃ with the valuation ring in the lattice-tree construction.
Residue-field cardinality, valuation factorization and the local PID argument.
Elementary-divisor forms of rank-two lattices after proving Z₃ is a PID.
Local compactness of Q₃ and compact openness of Z₃ under countable choice, covered by the corner theorem's AC assumption.
Existence of left Haar measure on the locally compact Hausdorff group under AC.
Right and inversion invariance of normalized Haar probability on I.
Explicit choice hypothesis of the selected p-adic convolution-corner theorem.
Existence and uniqueness of dominant-cone projection in positive dimension; the consumer handles dimension zero separately.
Projection-norm inequality and its equality case in strict parabolic weight decrease.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 says, “The subgroup I is open and closed in the compact space Z₃⁴, hence compact.” I is closed in Z₃⁴ but is not open there: every ambient neighborhood permits perturbing a matrix entry so that its determinant is no longer one. I is open in G. Closedness in Z₃⁴ already proves the required compactness, so this is an ambient-space wording correction and does not undermine the theorem.

seams_checked.note: Both pages distinguish reading context from logical suppliers. The affine page does not import the finite spectral R-matrix as an affine construction, and its unnormalized quadratic relation is compatible with the interface page's explicit generator rescaling.

The Cherednik page explicitly treats this as a reading-order edge and uses no batch-71 item as a logical supplier. Its finite Hecke/KZ claims do not invoke affine PBW or the affine Langlands classification.

The DAHA page accurately describes the general affine PBW theorem's positive-parameter scope, treats the prerequisite as a reading route, and supplies its A₁ DAHA and Macdonald arguments locally without extending the affine theorem to double-affine claims.
